# A maximum of admissible projective contact weights need not be repairable

This note checks the scope of the newly proposed projective-weighted
surface parity theorem. A common positive affine denominator can have
the required harmonic density envelope. Taking the actual maximum of
two source-specific projective erosion fields can destroy that envelope
by an arbitrarily large factor. Thus the common-denominator hypothesis
cannot be dropped when using the new theorem in a joint deformation.

Let n=1,d=2 and C=[-1,1] times K, where K=[-1,1]^2. Choose the sources
(-1,0) and (1,0), with 0 the ordinary centroid of K. Their ordinary
projective normalization parameter is a=0. Fix any b>0 and define

    L_-(z,x)=1+b(z+1), L_+(z,x)=1+b(1-z).

Both are positive on C and equal one on their respective source
fibers. With H(u)=h_K(u), their projective boundary potentials are

    Phi_-(u,z,x)=H(u)L_-(z,x)^(-2),
    Phi_+(u,z,x)=H(u)L_+(z,x)^(-2).

These are actual globally convex projective fields on a neighborhood
of C. They can be continued by the usual tangent extension outside
that neighborhood. Global supporting slopes are zero, so every fiber
is in contact with every source supporting plane. The actual joint
erosion formed by intersecting the two sets of convex cuts therefore
has speed max(Phi_-,Phi_+) on each regular boundary face, exactly as in
`candidate 6748c967393345b9`.

On the top edge, with u=(0,1) and H(u)=1, this maximum has the values

    F_-1=1, F_0=(1+b)^(-2), F_1=1.

All three top faces are copies of [-1,1] times {1}. Couple the full
length measures on the two endpoint top faces by identical continuous
coordinates. This is a normal-preserving integer-midpoint coupling
with midpoint on the actual middle support face. Every coupling of
these same endpoint measures has midpoint base zero and total mass2.
The proposed middle weighted capacity has total mass2/(1+b)^2.

Consequently no repair, with or without convex-order domination, can
have midpoint law dominated by that middle weighted capacity. Even
allowing a uniform multiplicative constant A would require

    A >= (1+b)^2.

There is no constant independent of b. In particular, putting b=1
requires A>=4, larger than the n=1 parity factor2.

For a single field the endpoint weights differ, and its harmonic
capacity estimate is not contradicted. Nor does this example rule out
choosing better source extensions: b=0 makes both fields coincide and
removes the obstruction in this product. What fails is the inference
that an arbitrary actual contact maximum inherits the density-repair
property of each of its constituent projective fields.
